_note: Day 8 shift: a web request arrives. Built by the generic path of LogGenerator (event "request"). 'Sent by' and 'Typed in' are info parts (who sends it, and which box, decide nothing). 'What was typed' is an "allowed" rule with "odd_values" (an apostrophe in a name is fine) and an "exempt" (our own scanner may type code: it is cleared, but worth a second look: the Day 8 engine addition). 'Answer' is an "allowed" rule. The threat is the code ' OR 1=1 -- typed into the login name, which repeats in bad logs.

comments.short: Joshua: No mistakes, but too few logs. Be quicker.

hud_line: Read what was typed    On call: {on_call}

rules.name: Sent by
rules.text: Who sends it decides nothing. A customer can be an attacker, and our own scanner is not one.
details: Ours: the security team's scanner, every Tuesday.
A customer may type anything into a box.
rules.why: Look at what was typed and what came back.

rules.name: Typed in
rules.text: The box decides nothing. Code can be typed into any box.
details: The login form, the search box and the order form all take text.
rules.why: Every box is a way in if its text is not checked.

rules.name: What was typed
rules.text: A name, a search or an order number is letters, digits and spaces. An apostrophe in a name is fine. Code is not.
details: Our own scanner may type code: it is testing us on purpose.
Look at the whole text, not at one character.
rules.why: Typed text is data. It must never be taken for an order.
rules.broken: has code in what was typed

rules.name: Answer
rules.text: A request gets back what it asked for: one row, a page, or a polite not found.
details: Thousands of rows or a database error means the site did something it should not.
rules.why: The answer shows what the website really did.
rules.broken: got back thousands of rows or a database error

decoys.reason: An apostrophe in a name is normal text: it is a customer called O'Brien, and the site showed his page.
That is the security team's own scanner, testing the site on purpose. It typed code, and the site refused it.
A long search is still letters and spaces. Nothing in it is code.

story_logs.reason: {first} typed his own name, with an apostrophe, and the site showed his page.
{first}'s team runs the scanner every Tuesday. It types code on purpose, and the site refused it.

ok: The sender, {by}, does not decide this.
Who sends it tells you little.

odd: An apostrophe or a long text is fine. Read all of it before you decide.
exempt: Code, but it comes from our own scanner. Look at who sent it.
bad: Read {typed} out loud. It is an order to the database.

ok: Getting {answer} is what a request should get.
bad: Getting {answer} means the site did something it should not.
{answer} is far more than anyone asked for.

1: New shift. Customers type into the website. Text is data, until a site takes it for an order. This time you read what was typed.
Click a line to ask me about it. The clock is frozen while you learn.
Rules are in the RULEBOOK. Then LET PASS or REPORT.
2: Check all four lines of the request.
3: An apostrophe is not an attack, and our own scanner types code on purpose. Read the whole text and who sent it.
4: The clock runs now. Good luck.

rulebook.intro: REPORT requests that break a rule. LET PASS the rest, even the ones that look odd.
rulebook.margin: Within %d of the limit is a bit odd, but still allowed.

messages.no_time: No time to ask. Decide now.
